column1: # AUTO-GENERATED by tools/datamine_area_tiers.py --emit -- DO NOT EDIT.
# Vanilla's own declared difficulty per play_region bucket: the weighted MEDIAN base-game
#   ladder rung (7010..7200 -> index 0..19) over every enemy Part vanilla PLACED on that
#   ground, read from NpcParam.spEffectID3.
# Replaces the LIVE census (er-logic::scaling::area_tier_from_histogram) as the primary
#   source for presumed_native_tier{,_down}. The live census + AreaAnchor stay as the
#   fallback for ground this table does not cover.
# WHY: the live census counts rung-AND-band carriers and our own sweep strips the band, so
#   it erases its own sample -- bobler 2026-08-09 saw `from 0 vanilla-shaped` on 33 of 48
#   sweeps of bucket 69300 and `left vanilla` never converged (122..214).
# tier is EMPTY where the sample is below MIN_AREA_SAMPLE (8) -- same floor as the client;
#   an empty tier means 'no claim', and the caller must fall back, NOT default to 0.
# dlc_rungs counts parts whose rung is the DLC re-emission (20007000..20007350), which is a
#   STEEPER curve at the same indices and is deliberately NOT folded in.
# TRACKED (tier-2, AGENTS.md 5a): needs MSBs, which are not in gen_inputs.db.
# ladder=dlc rows are ranked WITHIN the 16-rung DLC ladder and projected onto 0..19 by
#   RANK, because the two ladders are disjoint bands (base 1.141-7.422x HP, DLC
#   7.047-16.641x) and no multiplier mapping between them exists. A base tier and a DLC
#   tier are therefore NOT comparable to each other -- only each to its own region's
#   sphere target, which is what consumes them.
